:::{#exr-matrix-from-rows-practice}
#### Stacking rows into a matrix

@thm-matrix-column-of-rows says that a [matrix](#def-matrix) is determined by its [row](#def-matrix-row)s,
so data recorded one observation at a time
can be assembled into a matrix by stacking those records.
Let $\matr{M}$ be the $3 \times 2$ matrix with

$$
\matr{M}_{1,:} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{M}_{2,:} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{M}_{3,:} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

What is $\matr{M}_{:,2}$, the second [column of $\matr{M}$](#def-matrix-column)?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Stack the [row](#def-matrix-row)s from top to bottom, as in @thm-matrix-column-of-rows,
then read down the second [column](#def-matrix-column).

:::
